package.title: 100 NAT-IE Mechanics MCQs with Answers and Explanations

questions.question: Which quantity is a vector?
A car travels 150 m in 10 s at constant speed. What is its speed?
A runner moves 8 m east and then 3 m west along a straight track. What is the runner's displacement?
A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 6 s. What is its final velocity?
A vehicle moving at 20 m/s slows uniformly to 5 m/s in 3 s. What is its acceleration?
An object starts from rest and accelerates at 3 m/s² for 4 s. How far does it travel in that time?
A cyclist moving at 6 m/s accelerates at 2 m/s² over a distance of 16 m. What is the final speed?
A ball is dropped from rest and falls freely for 2 s. Taking g = 10 m/s² and neglecting air resistance, how far does it fall?
A stone is thrown vertically upward at 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², how long does it take to reach its highest point?
A ball is thrown vertically upward at 30 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², what maximum height does it reach above its starting point?
A car's velocity increases uniformly from 4 m/s to 16 m/s in 6 s. What is its average velocity during this interval?
On a velocity-time graph, what does the area between the graph and the time axis represent?
A particle moves with constant velocity in a straight line. What is its acceleration?
A displacement of 6 m east is followed by 8 m north. What is the magnitude of the net displacement?
A 2 kg object has a resultant force of 10 N acting on it. What is its acceleration?
A 5 kg box rests on a horizontal floor. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the normal force from the floor?
A 4 kg object is acted on by a 20 N force to the right and a 4 N force to the left. What is its acceleration?
A person pushes a wall with a force of 80 N. According to Newton's third law, what force does the wall exert on the person?
A 3 kg object is in free fall near Earth's surface. Taking g = 10 m/s² and neglecting air resistance, what is the gravitational force on it?
A 10 kg block is pulled horizontally by 30 N while 10 N of kinetic friction opposes its motion. What is its acceleration?
A 10 kg block rests on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction is 0.4 and g = 10 m/s². What is the maximum static friction force?
A 5 kg block slides on a horizontal surface with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.2. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the kinetic friction force?
A 2 kg object hangs at rest from a light vertical string. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the tension in the string?
Two blocks of masses 2 kg and 3 kg are connected by a light string on a frictionless horizontal surface. A 10 N horizontal force pulls the 3 kg block. What is the acceleration of the system?
A 4 kg mass hangs at rest from a vertical rope. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the rope tension?
An object rests on a frictionless incline that is 30° above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its acceleration down the incline?
A 2 kg object moves in a straight line at constant velocity. What is the net force on it?
A lift accelerates upward at 2 m/s². What is the apparent weight of a 50 kg passenger if g = 10 m/s²?
A lift accelerates downward at 3 m/s². What is the apparent weight of a 60 kg passenger if g = 10 m/s²?
A 2 kg object moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A 4 kg object is raised 5 m vertically. Taking g = 10 m/s², how much gravitational potential energy does it gain?
A constant force of 12 N moves an object 5 m in the same direction as the force. How much work is done?
A 20 N force acts perpendicular to an object's 3 m displacement. How much work does this force do?
A net force does 50 J of work on an object initially at rest. What is the object's final kinetic energy?
A 2 kg object initially at rest gains 36 J of kinetic energy. What is its final speed?
A machine does 600 J of work in 3 s. What is its average power?
A motor delivers 1000 W while lifting a load vertically at a steady speed of 2 m/s. What upward force does it exert?
A 2 kg object falls from rest through 5 m. Neglecting air resistance and taking g = 10 m/s², what speed does it have just before reaching the ground?
A 1 kg object moving at 4 m/s is brought to rest. What is the change in its kinetic energy?
A force of 5 N acts opposite to the displacement of an object through 4 m. What work does the force do?
A 3 kg object moves at 4 m/s. What is its momentum?
A 2 kg ball moving at 5 m/s is brought to rest in 0.5 s. What is the magnitude of the average force on it?
A 2 kg object moving at 4 m/s collides and sticks to a stationary 2 kg object. What is their common velocity immediately after the collision?
A 1 kg object moving east at 6 m/s collides with a 2 kg object at rest. They stick together. What is their velocity after collision?
A 0.2 kg ball changes velocity from 10 m/s east to 5 m/s west. What is the magnitude of its change in momentum?
A 3 kg object moving at 4 m/s has what momentum?
A 0.5 kg ball moving at 8 m/s is caught and stopped in 0.2 s. What is the magnitude of the average force exerted on it?
A 1 kg object moving at 6 m/s collides head-on with an identical object initially at rest. They stick together. What is their shared speed after collision?
A 2 kg object moving at 5 m/s collides with a 3 kg object moving in the same direction at 1 m/s. They stick together. What is their final velocity?
A 1 kg object moving east at 4 m/s collides with a stationary 3 kg object. They stick together. What is their velocity after collision?
A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s is acted on by a constant 4 N force in its direction of motion for 2 s. What is its final speed?
A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s is acted on by a constant 4 N force in the direction of motion over 5 m. What is its final speed?
A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s is acted on by a constant 4 N force in its direction of motion for 2 s. What is the change in its momentum?
A 1 kg object initially at rest receives an impulse of 6 N·s. What is its speed immediately afterward?
A 2 kg object moving at 4 m/s has what kinetic energy?
A 2 kg object moves at 4 m/s. What is its momentum?
A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s experiences a net force of 4 N in the same direction for 2 s. What is its final speed?
A 1 kg object moving at 5 m/s is acted on by a 3 N force in the direction of motion over 4 m. What is its final speed?
A 1 kg object moving at 4 m/s collides with a stationary 3 kg object and they stick together. What is the final speed?
A 2 kg object moves in a circle of radius 3 m at 6 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
A 2 kg object moves in a circle of radius 4 m at 6 m/s. What is the magnitude of the net centripetal force?
An object moves in a circle at constant speed. What is true of its velocity?
choices: It remains constant because speed is constant
It is always directed toward the centre
It is zero at every point

questions.question: A 0.5 kg object moves in a circle of radius 2 m at 4 m/s. What is its centripetal force?
A vehicle moves at 10 m/s around a level circular track of radius 20 m. What centripetal acceleration is required?
If the speed of an object in a circle doubles while the radius remains unchanged, how does its centripetal acceleration change?
choices: It becomes four times as large

questions.question: An object travels once around a circular track at constant speed. What is its displacement after the complete lap?
A wheel completes 5 revolutions in 10 s. What is its frequency?
A rotating object has a period of 0.25 s. What is its frequency?
An object moves at constant speed around a circle. In which direction does its instantaneous acceleration point?
choices: Toward the centre of the circle

questions.question: A body has mass 5 kg. What is its weight on Earth if g = 9.8 m/s²?
An astronaut's mass is 60 kg on Earth. What is the astronaut's mass on the Moon?
If the distance between two point masses is doubled, what happens to the magnitude of their gravitational force?
choices: It becomes four times as large

questions.question: A planet has the same radius as Earth but four times Earth's mass. If Earth's surface gravitational field is g, what is the planet's surface gravitational field?
A 2 kg object is 3 m above a chosen reference level. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its gravitational potential energy relative to that level?
A 2 kg object is raised vertically by 4 m at constant speed. Taking g = 10 m/s², how much work is done against gravity?
What is the SI unit of gravitational field strength?
At a point between two equal point masses, what is the net gravitational field due to the two masses?
choices: Twice the field from either mass in one direction

questions.question: A 2 kg object has a weight of 20 N in a gravitational field. What is the field strength?
An object is moved to a location where the gravitational field strength is half its original value. What happens to its weight?
choices: It becomes four times as large

questions.question: A 3 kg object is 2 m above a reference level. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its gravitational potential energy?
A force of 100 N acts uniformly over an area of 2 m². What pressure does it exert?
A liquid has density 1000 kg/m³. What is the gauge pressure 2 m below its surface if g = 10 m/s²?
A 0.02 m³ object is fully submerged in water of density 1000 kg/m³. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the buoyant force?
An object floats at rest in water. How does the buoyant force compare with the object's weight?
choices: It is smaller than the weight
It is greater than the weight

questions.question: A fluid flows through a pipe that narrows. For steady flow of an incompressible fluid, what happens to the fluid speed in the narrower section?
Water flows steadily through a pipe whose cross-sectional area changes from 4 cm² to 2 cm². If its speed in the wider section is 3 m/s, what is its speed in the narrower section?
A solid object has mass 600 g and volume 200 cm³. What is its density?
A 2 m² piston experiences a pressure of 5000 Pa. What force acts on it?
A hydraulic system has an input piston area of 0.01 m² and an output piston area of 0.2 m². If the input force is 50 N, what output force is produced in an ideal system?
A block has volume 0.01 m³ and is fully submerged in a liquid of density 800 kg/m³. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the buoyant force?
A liquid pressure is measured 1 m below its surface and again 3 m below its surface. For the same stationary liquid, how does the gauge pressure at 3 m compare with that at 1 m?
choices: It is three times as large
It is nine times as large

questions.question: A 3 kg object rests on a horizontal surface and exerts a force over an area of 0.5 m². Taking g = 10 m/s², what pressure does it exert?
For steady flow of an incompressible liquid through a pipe, what quantity remains constant along the pipe?
A spring extends 0.04 m when a force of 8 N is applied, within its elastic limit. What is its spring constant?
A spring with spring constant 100 N/m is compressed by 0.2 m. What elastic potential energy is stored?
A 2 kg object attached to a spring of spring constant 50 N/m is displaced 0.1 m from equilibrium. What is the magnitude of the restoring force?
A spring obeying Hooke's law is stretched from 2 cm to 4 cm. How does the magnitude of its restoring force change?
choices: It becomes four times as large

questions.question: A 2 kg object moves around a level circular path of radius 5 m at 10 m/s. What net inward force is required?
An object of mass 1 kg moves in a circle of radius 2 m at 4 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
A 4 kg object moves at 3 m/s in a circle of radius 2 m. What is the centripetal force?
